content.title: About
content.content: Slush frozen drink is a frozen beverage made from fruit juice, sugar and water, served as fine crystal “snow”. It is popular in summer, offers a bright flavor and a refreshing effect.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial Slush appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
There are more than 30 flavor variants, from classic cherry to exotic mango and passion fruit.
Special machines simultaneously freeze and stir the mixture, creating tiny crystals.
In some countries Slush is served in glasses with ice, in others in plastic cups with a straw.
Sugar content can reach 10–12 % of the total volume.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The water in Slush helps maintain fluid balance, especially in hot weather.

items.title: Vitamins and Antioxidants
items.content: Fruit juice provides vitamin C and other antioxidants that protect cells.

items.title: Energy Boost
items.content: Sugar quickly replenishes glucose stores, giving an instant energy lift.

items.title: Low Fat Content
items.content: Unlike many sweet drinks, Slush contains virtually no fat.

items.title: Mood Enhancement
items.content: The fresh fruit taste and cold sensation can improve mood and reduce fatigue.

items.title: High Sugar Content
items.content: Excessive consumption may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Allergy to Ingredients
items.content: Some flavors may contain nuts, dairy or artificial flavorings that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Cold Sensitivity
items.content: Drinking large amounts of a cold beverage can cause tooth or stomach discomfort in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Commercial versions often contain preservatives and artificial sweeteners that may not suit everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slush is served in a glass or cup, often with a straw. You can add fresh fruit, mint or lime juice to enhance the flavor. It is recommended to sip slowly to avoid over‑cooling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared Slush should be stored in a freezer at –18 °C for no more than 24 hours. With longer storage the texture may become too hard, so a brief thaw before serving is advisable.
